target: fatal accidents involving Boeing commercial jets

evidence.observation: IATA reports eight fatal accidents, including four fatal jet accidents with 213 onboard fatalities. The jet-fatality total maps to Ethiopian ET302 (157), Atlas Air 3591 (3), Aeroflot 1492/Sukhoi Superjet (41) and Bek Air/Fokker 100 (12). The first two are Boeing target members; the latter two are non-Boeing.

evidence.publisher: Ethiopian Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (EAIB); final report hosted by BEA France
evidence.authority_role: state accident-investigation authority / accredited-representative public host
evidence.source_title: Aircraft Accident Investigation Report B737-MAX 8 ET-AVJ
evidence.observation: Ethiopian Airlines ET302, Boeing 737 MAX 8 ET-AVJ, scheduled international passenger flight; 157 fatalities.

evidence.publisher: National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), United States
evidence.observation: Atlas Air flight 3591, Boeing 767-375BCF N1217A, operated as a Part 121 domestic cargo flight; captain, first officer and jumpseat pilot died.

completeness_assessment.reason: The IATA fatal-jet universe is mapped exhaustively to four jet cases and 213 onboard fatalities; the two Boeing target members have competent-authority evidence and the other two jet fatal accidents are non-Boeing. No unresolved target-taxonomy issue changes a 2019 Boeing membership decision.
